replication.target_description: Hull et al. (2002), Study 1a: elderly versus neutral scrambled-sentence priming, walking time, and private self-consciousness. Narrative discussion explicitly covers both Studies 1a and 1b. No new effect-size or p extraction is assigned.

reported_success.location: p. 409 (PDF p. 4), Studies 1a and 1b—Discussion, opening paragraph
reported_success.quote: Across two studies, individuals who were high in private self- ... consciousness but not those who were low in self-consciousness ... showed greater responsivity to a manipulation that is typically ... interpreted as affecting behavior in an automatic fashion.

notes: Only assigned unfinished fields are completed. All other fields are placeholders. The narrative verdict is coded mixed because the authors explicitly describe greater prime responsiveness for high but not low self-conscious participants; this is a conditional author conclusion, not a verdict inferred from p values. The combined-analysis statement that the prime effect replicates Bargh et al. is not treated as a separate-study unconditional verdict. Target-match identifies the study/outcome supporting assigned fields only, not any unassigned statistic.
